planners.name: astar
planners.summary: A*: priority = g + h. Cost-optimal with an admissible heuristic.

planners.name: awastar
planners.summary: Weighted A* that keeps going, lowering the weight after each solution.

planners.name: beam
planners.summary: Breadth-first search that keeps only the ``width`` best nodes per layer.

planners.name: bfs
planners.summary: FIFO breadth-first graph search. Optimal in number of actions.

planners.name: dfs
planners.summary: LIFO depth-first graph search. Complete on finite spaces, not optimal.

planners.name: dijkstra
planners.summary: Dijkstra's algorithm: priority = g. Cost-optimal, uninformed.

planners.name: ehc
planners.summary: Enforced hill climbing: breadth-first probes for a strictly better h.

planners.name: gbfs
planners.summary: Greedy best-first: priority = h. Fast but not optimal.

planners.name: hc
planners.summary: Steepest-ascent hill climbing with a sideways-move allowance.

planners.name: idastar
planners.summary: IDA*: depth-first search bounded by an increasing ``f = g + h`` threshold.

planners.name: iddfs
planners.summary: Iterative-deepening DFS. Shortest in plan length, with low memory.

planners.name: iw
planners.summary: Iterated Width: blind search pruned by *novelty*.

planners.name: wastar
planners.summary: Weighted A*: priority = g + w * h. Bounded-suboptimal for w > 1.

requirements.name: :action-costs
requirements.note: Operator costs feed straight into g, so A*/Dijkstra optimise cost. `k` is a constant or an expression over static functions, such as `(road-length ?from ?to)`, evaluated from `:init` when the action is grounded; one that reads a function some effect changes is refused. Under a metric over `(total-cost)` an action with no cost effect is free, as in IPC planners; under one over `(total-time)` an action costs its duration; under one that mentions neither, every action is free; without a metric every action costs 1 (a durative one, its duration). The metric must be `minimize` over `(total-cost)` or `(total-time)`, plus constant multiples of `(is-violated p)` and constants; `maximize` and any other shape are refused. A cost inside `when` and a negative cost are refused.

requirements.name: :conditional-effects
requirements.note: Kept explicitly in the grounded operator and evaluated against the state at application time.

requirements.name: :derived-predicates
requirements.note: Rules are grounded and re-evaluated from scratch to a least fixpoint after every state change, so planners and heuristics always see closed states and a derived fact whose support goes away is retracted. Negating a derived predicate in a precondition or goal is supported; negating one inside another rule, which needs stratification, is refused. Derived predicates may not appear in action effects.

requirements.name: :equality
requirements.note: Evaluated during grounding; infeasible instances are dropped.

requirements.name: :strips
requirements.note: The core representation. Everything else compiles down to this.

requirements.name: :typing
requirements.note: Subtypes are resolved transitively when building the object pools. `(either a b)` types are refused; declare a common supertype instead.
requirements.summary: Typed parameters and objects, with type hierarchies.

requirements.name: :disjunctive-preconditions
requirements.note: Preconditions are converted to DNF; each disjunct becomes its own grounded operator. A disjunctive goal becomes a single artificial goal fact achieved by one zero-cost operator per disjunct.

requirements.name: :duration-inequalities
requirements.note: Bounds are collected and the shortest feasible duration is chosen. With no concurrency and no continuous change nothing in the model prefers a longer action, so the tightest lower bound is makespan-optimal. Strict `<`/`>` are refused: they have no shortest feasible value.
requirements.summary: Durations bounded by inequalities rather than fixed.

requirements.name: :existential-preconditions
requirements.note: Expanded over the typed object pool into a disjunction, then handled like any other disjunction.

requirements.name: :negative-preconditions
requirements.note: Compiled to positive normal form: each negated fluent gets a complement fact that every operator maintains.

requirements.name: :universal-preconditions
requirements.note: Expanded over the typed object pool into a conjunction.

requirements.name: :constraints
requirements.note: `always`, `at-end`, `sometime`, `sometime-before`, `sometime-after` and `at-most-once` are compiled into invariants on every action, monitor facts and extra goal conjuncts; the monitors also watch the states timed literals fire in. A constraint under `forall` becomes one constraint per object. The metric-time forms (`within`, `always-within`, `hold-after`, `hold-during`) are refused by name, and so is any form but `always` and `at-end` when a durative action has at-start effects: its monitor cannot see the state between that action's start and end.

requirements.name: :durative-actions
requirements.note: Compiled to one sequential action each. At-start conditions are checked in the state the action starts in; over-all and at-end conditions in the state after its at-start effects (they are regressed through those effects when grounding). The at-start effects apply first and the at-end effects after them, so an at-end effect wins a conflict. The duration is carried through so plans report a makespan, and a `(total-time)` metric minimises it. Actions therefore never overlap — this models sequential temporal planning, not true concurrency, so a plan needing two actions to run at the same time will not be found. Refused: every effect and condition needs a time specifier (put a `when` inside one: `(at end (when c e))`); an at-start numeric effect that a later condition or effect of the same action reads; an at-end `when` that deletes what the at-start effects add, or reads a fact an at-start `when` may change.

requirements.name: :fluents
requirements.note: Both halves are implemented; see the two rows above for what each one covers.

requirements.name: :numeric-fluents
requirements.note: Supported: ground numeric fluents, comparisons (< <= = >= >) in preconditions and goals, and assign/increase/decrease/scale-up/scale-down effects over arithmetic expressions. Numeric values are part of the state, so the state space can become infinite — the delete-relaxation heuristics ignore numeric conditions, which keeps them admissible but uninformative about them.
requirements.summary: Numeric state variables, comparisons and assignments.

requirements.name: :object-fluents
requirements.note: Compiled to a predicate plus a uniqueness rule: `(= (location ?p) ?x)` becomes a fact and `assign` clears the old value first, in preconditions, effects, goals and trajectory constraints alike. Using an object fluent as a *nested term* — `(at ?t (location ?p))` — or as the value of another, as in `(assign (location ?p) (location ?q))`, is refused; write the equality form with a variable instead.
requirements.summary: Functions returning objects rather than numbers.

requirements.name: :preferences
requirements.note: Goal preferences are compiled into a priced choice: a closing action freezes the state, then each preference is resolved either for free (if it holds) or at its `(is-violated p)` weight, so cost-optimal search minimises the metric. Timed literals cannot fire after the closing action. A preference under `forall` is one preference per object, each priced at the name's weight. Under a metric, a preference it does not mention costs nothing to violate; without one, each costs 1. Preferences over trajectory constraints, inside action preconditions, or under `or`, `not`, `imply` or `exists` are refused.
requirements.summary: Soft goals scored by a metric.

requirements.name: :timed-initial-literals
requirements.note: Elapsed time becomes a numeric fluent advanced by action durations. Each literal gets a firing action guarded on the clock plus a wait action that advances it, and every domain action — and the end of the plan — is blocked while a due literal has not fired. Because actions never overlap, a literal scheduled strictly inside an action's duration fires immediately after that action rather than during it. A `(total-time)` metric is refused here: waiting takes time no action is charged for.
requirements.summary: Facts that become true (or false) at a given absolute time.

requirements.name: :continuous-effects
requirements.note: Requires continuous-time reasoning, which this planner does not do.
requirements.summary: Effects that change continuously over an action's duration.

requirements.name: :domain-axioms
requirements.note: Superseded by `:derived-predicates`, which is supported: write each axiom as a `(:derived ...)` rule.

requirements.name: :safety-constraints
requirements.note: Superseded by PDDL 3 trajectory constraints: `(:constraints (always ...))` says the same thing and is supported.

requirements.name: :ucpop
requirements.note: Refused because two of its parts are; declare `:adl` (and `:derived-predicates` for axioms) instead.
requirements.summary: The PDDL 1.2 UCPOP bundle: `:adl` plus `:domain-axioms` and `:safety-constraints`.
